title: Review the Exact Change
concept: Distinguish changed, added and deleted paths

writing.summary: Distinguish changed, added and deleted paths.
writing.rule: Compare source snapshots by path and content before selecting a commit.
writing.explanation:
A worktree is the collection you are editing. A commit records a particular tree; autosave protects edits but does not create a commit. Review both before selecting paths. A file can disappear, appear, or keep its name while its contents change. Looking only for new names misses modifications and deletions.

Build the candidate path set from both trees and compare values. Return each changed path once in lexical order. File ordering is presentation, not Git object identity. This lab models text trees; real Git also stores modes and opaque bytes. In the native terminal, inspect actual history through the existing libgit2-backed commands. The selected-path commit profile commits exactly the reviewed paths, so unrelated edits stay uncommitted.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run git status and git diff src/main.rs before committing. The terminal uses real Git; the lab isolates the tree-comparison contract.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises distinguish changed, added and deleted paths. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Return the sorted unique paths whose contents differ between two trees; include additions and deletions. Each input has unique paths. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: An existing file keeps its name but changes content. Should it appear in the review?
answers: Autosave makes the edit a commit
Yes, content is part of the snapshot
Only newly named files belong in a change review
writing.feedback: Comparing only path names misses modified content; comparing only the new tree misses deletions.

depth.misconception: Only newly named files belong in a change review
depth.correction: Compare source snapshots by path and content before selecting a commit.
